title: [MPS][AOTI] Check shader-library shim return codes in generated wrapper
body:
Fixes #196233.

## Summary

`cpp_wrapper_mps.py` generated AOTI code that ignored the return codes from:

- `aoti_torch_mps_create_shader_library`
- `aoti_torch_mps_get_kernel_function`

When shader compilation failed, `aoti_torch_mps_create_shader_library` returned an error without initializing `library_handle`. The generated wrapper then passed the null handle to `aoti_torch_mps_get_kernel_function`, causing a SIGSEGV and discarding the original Metal compiler diagnostic.

Wrap both calls with `AOTI_TORCH_ERROR_CODE_CHECK`, matching every other `cpp_wrapper` backend (`cpp_wrapper_cpu.py`, `cpp_wrapper_cpu_array_ref.py`, `cpp_wrapper_gpu.py`) and the hand-written consumer of this same shim API in `test/cpp_extensions/libtorch_agn_2_14_extension/csrc/mps/mps_set_arg_bytes_test.cpp`, which wraps every one of these calls. `cpp_wrapper_mps.py` was the only `cpp_wrapper` backend that did not reference the macro at all.

Also move the shader-library handle into its `unique_ptr` immediately after a successful create call. With the new error check, ownership must be established before the subsequent kernel-function lookup to avoid leaking the library on failure.

Update the `codegen_additional_funcs` docstring to match the generated code.

## Test plan

```bash
python test/inductor/test_mps_basic.py MPSBasicTestsAOTI.test_shader_compile_error_raises
python test/inductor/test_mps_basic.py MPSBasicTestsAOTI.test_kernel_function_lookup_error_raises
python test/inductor/test_mps_basic.py
python test/inductor/test_aot_inductor.py AOTInductorTestABICompatibleMps
spin quicklint
```

### Regression coverage

One test per shim call. Each forces a real failure and asserts the diagnostic
reaches Python; each segfaults without the fix.

- `test_shader_compile_error_raises` injects invalid MSL, so
  `aoti_torch_mps_create_shader_library` fails.
- `test_kernel_function_lookup_error_raises` renames the kernel symbol, so the
  library compiles but `aoti_torch_mps_get_kernel_function` cannot find
  `generated_kernel`. This covers the second call, which the first test never
  reaches because it fails earlier.

Before this change both segfault with no output:

```bash
$ python test/inductor/test_mps_basic.py MPSBasicTestsAOTI.test_shader_compile_error_raises; echo "exit=$?"
exit=139
$ python test/inductor/test_mps_basic.py MPSBasicTestsAOTI.test_kernel_function_lookup_error_raises; echo "exit=$?"
exit=139
```

After:

```bash
$ python test/inductor/test_mps_basic.py MPSBasicTestsAOTI.test_shader_compile_error_raises MPSBasicTestsAOTI.test_kernel_function_lookup_error_raises
..
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Ran 2 tests in 4.642s

OK
```

### Results

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `test/inductor/test_mps_basic.py` | 63 run, 63 passed |
| `test/inductor/test_aot_inductor.py` (MPS class) | 386 run: 196 passed, 157 skipped, 33 expected failures |
| `spin quicklint` | Passed |

## Environment

- macOS 15.5, arm64
- Apple M4 Pro
- `2.15.0a0+gitf62c80c`, built from source
- No CUDA available; non-MPS `test_aot_inductor.py` device classes were not run locally

Note: #195587 currently prevents editable builds from resolving shader `#include`s because `torch/include` is absent. Full-suite results above used a local `torch/include/c10 -> ../../c10` symlink. Without that workaround, Metal shader compilation fails due to the unrelated issue; this PR now reports the shim error rather than segfaulting. The two regression tests pass with or without the workaround.

## BC-breaking?

No. Successful generated code is unchanged; only error handling on failure paths changes.

## Follow-ups

Out of scope for this PR:

- Add return-code checks for other emitted `aoti_torch_mps_*` calls.
- Fix JIT `cpp_wrapper` on MPS, which currently fails on main with `undeclared identifier 'get_mps_lib_0_handle'`.

***

The implementation was prepared with an AI assistant (Claude) and reviewed and validated by the author. The reproduction, negative control, and suite runs were executed locally on the environment above.
